content: $\mathbb{T} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| = 1\}$. It is a compact metric space with the topology induced by $\mathbb{C}$. It is a multiplicative group with unit $e=1$ and $z^{-1} = \overline{z}$.

$C(\mathbb{T})$ is the space of continuous functions $f: \mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$, identified with $\{f \in C([-\pi, \pi]) : f(\pi) = f(-\pi)\}$. The subspace $\Pi(\mathbb{T}) = \{f(t) = \sum_{k=-M}^{N} \alpha_k e^{ikt} : N, M \in \mathbb{N}, \alpha_k \in \mathbb{C}\}$ is the space of trigonometric polynomials.

$C(\mathbb{T})$ is a Banach algebra with point-wise multiplication and the supremum norm $||f||_{\infty} = \sup_{t \in [-\pi, \pi)} |f(t)|$. The space of trigonometric polynomials $\Pi(\mathbb{T})$ is dense in $C(\mathbb{T})$.

A function $f: \mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is Lebesgue integrable if it is Lebesgue measurable and $\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} |f(t)| \frac{dt}{2\pi} < \infty$. $L^1(\mathbb{T})$ is the space of equivalence classes of such functions.
$L^1(\mathbb{T})$ is a Banach space equipped with the norm $||f||_1 = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi} |f(t)| \frac{dt}{2\pi}$.
Simple functions $S(\mathbb{T})$, continuous functions $C(\mathbb{T})$, and trigonometric polynomials $\Pi(\mathbb{T})$ are all dense in $L^1(\mathbb{T})$.

A set function $\lambda: \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{T}) \rightarrow [0, \infty]$ is a non-negative measure if $\lambda(\emptyset) = 0$ and it is countably additive for disjoint sets. It is regular if for any Borel set $A$ and $\epsilon > 0$, there exist a compact $K$ and open $G$ ($K \subset A \subset G$) such that $\lambda(G \setminus K) < \epsilon$.

A set function $\mu: \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{T}) \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is a complex measure if it is countably additive. Its variation $|\mu|$ on $A$ is $\sup \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} |\mu(A_n)|$ over all countable disjoint Borel partitions of $A$.
For a complex measure $\mu$, its variation $|\mu|$ is a non-negative measure, and it is the smallest non-negative measure $\lambda$ satisfying $|\mu(E)| \le \lambda(E)$ for all Borel sets $E$.
For any $z_1, ..., z_n \in \mathbb{C}$, there exists a subset $S \subset \{1, ..., n\}$ such that $|\sum_{j \in S} z_j| \ge \frac{1}{6} \sum_{j=1}^n |z_j|$.
If $\mu$ is a complex measure, then its variation $|\mu|$ is a finite measure (i.e., $|\mu|(\mathbb{T}) < \infty$).

For $f \in L^1(\mathbb{T})$, the set function $\mu(E) = \int_E f(t) \frac{dt}{2\pi}$ is a regular complex measure, its variation is $|\mu|(E) = \int_E |f(t)| \frac{dt}{2\pi}$, and $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure $m$.
